classification.difficultyReason: Check two junctions and sketch three joined lines, then substitute −x, reverse the branch inequalities and match the reordered expressions to −f(x).

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1$ and $x=1$.

answer.short: At $x=-1$, both branch values and $f(-1)$ equal $1$. At $x=1$, both branch values and $f(1)$ equal $-1$. Hence $f$ is continuous at both junctions.
answer.worked: At $x=-1$: $$\begin{align*}f(-1)&=-(-1)=1\\\text{Left branch at }-1&=-1+2=1\\\text{Right branch at }-1&=-(-1)=1\end{align*}$$At $x=1$: $$\begin{align*}f(1)&=-1\\\text{Left branch at }1&=-1\\\text{Right branch at }1&=1-2=-1\end{align*}$$At each junction the branch values equal the function value, so $f$ is continuous at both junctions.
